scenes.heading: Elements and the periodic table
scenes.sub: Everything is built from just over a hundred elements
scenes.say: The air you breathe and the phone in your pocket are made from just over a hundred elements. Let's see what atoms are made of, and how the periodic table organises them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A marble on the centre square of the MCG
scenes.science: A tiny, dense nucleus in a mostly empty atom
scenes.breaks: electrons aren't specks in the seats; they're a spread-out cloud of negative charge attracted to the nucleus.
scenes.say: Blow an atom up to the size of the MCG. The nucleus would be a marble on the centre square, with electrons out in the stands. Yet that marble holds almost all the mass, because protons and neutrons are each about eighteen hundred and thirty-six times heavier than an electron.
scenes.caption: Blow an atom up to the size of the MCG. The nucleus would be a marble on the centre square, with electrons out in the stands. Yet that marble holds almost all the mass, because protons and neutrons are each about 1836 times heavier than an electron.

scenes.heading: Inside the atom
scenes.say: Protons are positive and neutrons have no charge; both sit in the nucleus. Electrons are negative and sit around it. The atomic number, Z, counts protons and tells you which element it is. The mass number, A, is protons plus neutrons. So neutrons equal A minus Z.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in the ion ⁵⁶Fe³⁺?
scenes.say: How many particles are in iron fifty-six with a three plus charge? Iron's atomic number is twenty-six, so twenty-six protons. Neutrons are fifty-six minus twenty-six, which is thirty. The three plus charge means three electrons were lost, leaving twenty-three electrons.
scenes.caption: How many particles are in ⁵⁶Fe³⁺? Iron's atomic number is 26, so 26 protons. Neutrons are 56 − 26 = 30. The 3+ charge means 3 electrons were lost, leaving 23 electrons.

scenes.heading: Isotopes
scenes.say: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons. Chlorine thirty-five and chlorine thirty-seven both have seventeen protons, but eighteen and twenty neutrons. Same electrons means same chemistry; only the mass differs.

scenes.heading: Relative atomic mass
scenes.say: Relative atomic mass is a weighted average of the isotopes. Multiply each isotope's mass by its percentage abundance, add them up and divide by one hundred. The answer leans towards the most common isotope, which is why chlorine is thirty-five point four five.
scenes.caption: Relative atomic mass is a weighted average of the isotopes. Multiply each isotope's mass by its % abundance, add them up and divide by 100. The answer leans towards the most common isotope, which is why chlorine is 35.45.

scenes.heading: The periodic table
points: Periods go across: number of shells
scenes.say: The periodic table is ordered by atomic number. Elements in the same group, going down, have similar chemistry. The period number, going across, tells you how many shells are occupied.

points: Aᵣ is a weighted average of isotopes
scenes.say: Quick recap. Neutrons equal mass number minus atomic number. Losing electrons makes a positive ion, gaining them makes a negative ion. Isotopes differ only in neutrons. Relative atomic mass is a weighted average. Now try the practice questions!
